findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — A successful ordinary Google refresh persists the safeParse result envelope as the credential key, leaving subsequent calendar instances without top-level OAuth tokens.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Shared refresh returns a Fetch Response instead of the SDK token objects expected by Google and HubSpot, so successful parent responses cannot update their access tokens.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed Zod property names strip real expiry fields from shared responses, leaving Outlook credentials expired and forcing another parent refresh on every request.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — An ordinary Outlook refresh response without the optional refresh_token overwrites the stored valid token with the literal refresh_token, breaking the next refresh.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62 — Shared Webex responses containing the documented access token and expiry fail the unchanged schema requiring scope and refresh credentials, preventing meeting operations after expiration.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The sync path returns a native Fetch Response even though Google and HubSpot callers consume provider-specific parsed objects, so a configured parent sync cannot supply their expected token fields and refreshes fail.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6 — The computed Zod keys stringify to a literal "[object Object]", so sync parsing strips expiry and provider metadata and persists credentials that Office365/Salesforce can no longer refresh correctly.
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Persisting the safeParse result instead of its data nests Google tokens under data and makes the next credential load fail validation.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Returning a raw fetch Response in sync mode breaks Google and HubSpot callers that read SDK token fields directly instead of parsing JSON.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed Zod string keys are literal property names rather than wildcard validators, so sync parsing drops expiry and refresh fields and leaves Outlook credentials expired.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Substituting the literal refresh_token when an Outlook refresh response omits that optional field overwrites the saved valid token and breaks subsequent refreshes.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — The new credential update references prisma without importing or defining it, preventing Salesforce client initialization after a successful refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The any return boundary hides incompatible fetch and SDK responses, breaking Google and HubSpot shared refreshes; normalize both branches to a typed token contract.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every Salesforce service construction now refreshes and writes the credential even when its token is valid, adding remote and database work to each calendar operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47 — Any accepted team member can attach OAuth credentials through a forged teamId because the team branch returns before the admin permission check.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — No tests exercise the new credential-sync webhook's authorization, validation, and create-versus-update paths, so a regression can ship undetected

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — No tests cover the new parent-sync refresh branch or its provider-refresh fallback, so enabled deployments can regress credential renewal without detection

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
